strategies.subject: Physics
common_traps: Confusing reference frames in relative motion
Forgetting pseudo forces in non-inertial frames
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Energy Method**: When forces are complex, use energy conservation. Work-energy theorem is often faster than Newton's laws for problems involving variable forces.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 11 Chapters 3-7 cover mechanics. JEE expects deeper problem-solving skills beyond NCERT.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 5-7 questions per paper. Often combined with calculus. NLM + circular motion is common.

strategies.subject: Physics
common_traps: Confusing electric field and potential formulas
Sign errors in work done by electric field
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Potential Method**: For complex charge configurations, calculate potential first (scalar), then field if needed. This avoids vector addition.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 12 Chapters 1-3. JEE tests circuit analysis skills heavily.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 4-6 questions. RC circuits and Gauss's law are favorites.

strategies.subject: Physics
common_traps: Confusing binding energy per nucleon trends
Confusing activity with number of atoms
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Ratio Method**: For radioactivity problems, always work with ratios (N/N₀, A/A₀). Avoid absolute calculations when possible.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 12 Chapters 11-13. JEE tests numerical applications.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 3-4 questions. Photoelectric effect and nuclear physics common.

strategies.subject: Chemistry
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Mechanism First**: Always draw the mechanism. Identify: (1) nucleophile, (2) electrophile, (3) leaving group. This predicts products accurately.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 12 Chapters 10-16. JEE expects mechanism understanding.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 10-12 questions. Reaction mechanisms and named reactions dominate.

strategies.subject: Chemistry
common_traps: Unit conversion errors (especially in gas laws)
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Dimensional Analysis**: Always check units. If answer has wrong units, the method is wrong. This catches 90% of calculation errors.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 11 Chapters 1-7, Class 12 Chapters 1-5. JEE needs numerical proficiency.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 10-12 questions. Electrochemistry and equilibrium are high-weightage.

strategies.subject: Mathematics
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Substitution Strategy**: For integration, always check if u-substitution works first. 70% of JEE integrals can be solved by substitution alone.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 12 Chapters 5-8. JEE expects mastery of all techniques.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 10-12 questions. Definite integrals and application of derivatives common.

strategies.subject: Mathematics
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Pattern Recognition**: In sequences, always check if it's AP, GP, or AGP. For matrices, check if special properties apply (symmetric, orthogonal).
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 11 Chapters 4-9, Class 12 Chapters 3-4. JEE adds complexity.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 8-10 questions. Matrices and quadratics are favorites.

strategies.subject: Biology
common_traps: Confusing different types of blood cells
Mixing up hormone sources and targets
strategies.shortcut_technique: **System-by-System**: Study each body system completely before moving to next. Use flowcharts for processes like digestion, respiration.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 11 Chapters 17-22, Class 12 Chapters 16-19. NEET directly tests NCERT content.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 15-20 questions. Diagrams are crucial. Focus on NCERT figures.

strategies.subject: Biology
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Punnett Square Practice**: Do 10 pedigree problems daily. For molecular biology, memorize the enzymes and their functions.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 12 Chapters 5-7. NEET expects application skills.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 12-15 questions. Pedigree analysis and molecular biology common.

strategies.subject: Biology
common_traps: Confusing C3 vs C4 vs CAM plants
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Diagram-First Approach**: For plant anatomy, always start by drawing the diagram. Label all parts. This helps in MCQ elimination.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 11 Chapters 5-15, Class 12 Chapters 2-3, 13-15. NCERT figures are gold.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 20-25 questions. Photosynthesis and plant anatomy are high-weightage.

strategies.subject: Physics
strategies.shortcut_technique: **NCERT Numerical Focus**: NEET physics is formula-based. Memorize formulas and practice NCERT back-of-chapter numericals.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 11 Chapters 3-7. NEET tests direct NCERT content.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 8-10 questions. Direct formula application is common.

strategies.subject: Chemistry
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Functional Group Mastery**: Learn reactions grouped by functional group. Make a table: Functional Group → Reagent → Product.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 12 Chapters 10-16. NEET directly tests NCERT reactions.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 15-18 questions. Named reactions and conversions are favorites.

strategies.subject: Physics
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Circuit Simplification**: Always simplify circuits to series-parallel combinations. Redraw complex circuits step by step.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 10 Chapter 12, Class 12 Chapters 3-5. CBSE follows NCERT exactly.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 10-12 marks. Circuit numericals and magnetic effect of current common.

strategies.subject: Chemistry
strategies.shortcut_technique: **Balance First**: Always balance equations before answering. Check: atoms balanced, charges balanced (for ionic), conditions written.
strategies.ncert_relevance: NCERT Class 10 Chapters 1-4, Class 12 Chapters 1-8. Direct NCERT testing.
strategies.pyq_pattern: 8-10 marks. Balancing and identifying reaction types common.
